name: 3d-card

frames.best_why: The card is fully in view and clearly tilted in perspective, with no cursor over the content.

tagline: Card tips in 3D toward the pointer and its layers pull apart.
summary: A dark product card whose body rotates toward the cursor while the title, paragraph, photo and buttons sit at separate depths. Move away and it eases back flat.
appearance: A rounded near-black card on a black stage, outlined by a faint border. Inside sit a bold white title, a short grey paragraph, a wide forest photo in a rounded frame, and a footer row with a plain text link at left and a white pill button at right.
behaviour: Moving the pointer over the card tips it toward the cursor; the heading, text, image and buttons each hold a different depth, so they fan apart as it turns. Leaving the card smoothly resets it to flat.
demo_content: "Make things float in air", a forest photo, a Try now link and a Sign up button.
search_phrases: card that tilts toward your mouse
image card that follows the cursor
use_when: A showcase card should feel physical and reward hovering, as on portfolios, product pages or feature grids.
avoid_when: Touch screens never fire the hover tilt, and there is no reduced-motion fallback for sensitive users.
customise: Set each layer's depth with translateX/Y/Z and rotateX/Y/Z, and restyle via className on container, body and items. Text, image and links are your own children.
weight_why: Three small wrappers and CSS transforms on pointer move; nothing loops.

a11y.note: Tilt is pointer-only with no keyboard equivalent and no reduced-motion check, so keyboard users never see the effect.

issues: Description wraps with 'perspective' alone on a second line.
polish_why: Card reads clearly and the tilt is convincing; the orphaned word is a small flaw.
